history.name: The printed edition for the client
history.description: The command ledger build prints a PDF of one release: a front page carrying the masthead, the feature count, a bar breaking those features down by size, and a note of what changed since the last edition, then every entry in reading order. The document is real HTML and CSS, printed through the Chrome or Edge already on the machine, with the two fonts embedded so text copies cleanly out of the finished file. Any edition can be reprinted at any time, and it reproduces exactly what was presented that day.
history.dev_notes: src/render/ledger-html.mjs builds the document, src/render/pdf.mjs drives Chromium via playwright-core (channel chrome, msedge, chromium, or $LEDGER_CHROME). Fonts are static instances, not variable ones, or Chromium emits Type 3 glyphs that copy out shredded; After rendering, pdf.mjs asks Chromium (CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode) which font drew each element's text and fails the build if any is a system font; Noto Sans Symbols 2 is embedded last in both stacks for quoted UI icons. `--version N|all` picks the edition, `--html` writes the page instead of printing it.

history.description: The command ledger build prints a PDF of one release: a front page carrying the masthead, the feature count, a bar breaking those features down by size, and a note of what changed since the last edition, then a contents list that links into the document, then every entry in reading order. The document is real HTML and CSS, printed through the Chrome or Edge already on the machine, with the two fonts embedded so text copies cleanly out of the finished file. An edition can print a different version number from the one the ledger counts by: set display_version on a release in releases.json, and that edition and every later one are numbered on from it. Any edition can be reprinted at any time, and it reproduces exactly what was presented that day.
changes: The contents list was a printed index: it named each area and how many features were in it, but reaching a section meant scrolling for it. Every line is now a link to the section it names, and the closing sections on what was withdrawn and what else changed are listed there too, because the edition is usually read on screen rather than on paper.

Every edition printed the ledger's own version number, starting from 1, so a project whose client already held reports sent another way before the ledger started handed them a second Version 1. A release can now set the number its edition prints, and later editions carry on from it; the ledger's own numbering is unchanged.
history.dev_notes: src/render/ledger-html.mjs builds the document, src/render/pdf.mjs drives Chromium via playwright-core (channel chrome, msedge, chromium, or $LEDGER_CHROME). Contents entries are plain <a href="#id"> anchors onto ids on the area heads (area-N) and the closing sections (closing-*); Chromium turns those into named destinations in the PDF, so nothing has to position links by hand. Fonts are static instances, not variable ones, or Chromium emits Type 3 glyphs that copy out shredded; After rendering, pdf.mjs asks Chromium (CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode) which font drew each element's text and fails the build if any is a system font; Noto Sans Symbols 2 is embedded last in both stacks for quoted UI icons. `--version N|all` picks the edition, `--html` writes the page instead of printing it. The printed number comes from ReleaseSet.labelOf, which carries the nearest earlier display_version forward; it reaches the cover, footer, colophon, title, redraft note and pdf_name, and nothing else — `--version` and every `version` in the corpus stay the real number.
